user_query.title: Recover Bayesian Network DAG and Perform Causal Intervention on Y
user_query.text:
Recover the underlying DAG from the Bayesian Network data sample at /app/bn_sample_10k.csv. The original DAG has U with no parents and exactly six total edges; for any edge not involving U whose direction is unclear, assume the node labeled with the letter that comes first alphabetically is the child of the node that comes second. Save the recovered DAG edges to /app/learned_dag.csv in the format:
to,from
A,B
C,D
...
Then learn a Bayesian Network from /app/bn_sample_10k.csv using the recovered DAG, perform a causal intervention on Y setting its value to 0.0 (if an exact-value intervention is unavailable, use an extremely small variance around 0.0, stated as 10e-9), save the intervened BN edges to /app/intervened_dag.csv in the same format, sample 10,000 points from the intervened BN, and save the result to /app/final_bn_sample.csv with the same column names as the original data.

events.thought:
Analysis: bnlearn works. PC/GS skeleton has 7 edges (U-Y, U-R, U-D, U-M, R-M, D-Y, M-Y), but true DAG has 6. HC found exactly 6 edges: U->R, U->M, U->Y, U->D, Y->D, R->M (dropping M-Y). Need to determine which edge is spurious: M-Y (HC's choice) or U-M (alternative where M's parents are Y,R). I'll run conditional independence tests and compare BIC scores of candidate 6-edge DAGs.
Plan: Run CI tests (M⊥Y|U, U⊥M|{Y,R}, etc.) and score candidate DAGs with BIC-g to pick the best 6-edge DAG.

cat('M_Y|U,R: '); print(ci.test('M','Y',c('U','R'),data=df)$p.value)

events.thought:
Analysis: BIC clearly favors DAG A: [U][Y|U][R|U][D|U:Y][M|U:R] with score -193627.6 (best). The edges are U->Y, U->R, U->D, U->M, Y->D, R->M. This matches the hints: U has no parents, 6 edges total, and the two non-U edges (D-Y, M-R) oriented with alphabetically-first node as child (D child of Y, M child of R). Now I need to save the learned DAG, fit a Gaussian BN, perform a mutilation intervention setting Y=0, save the intervened DAG, and sample 10k points.
Plan: Write an R script: define DAG A, write learned_dag.csv (to,from format), fit with bn.fit, apply mutilated() with evidence Y=0 (this removes Y's incoming edges and sets Y constant at 0), write intervened_dag.csv, sample 10k via rbn, and save final_bn_sample.csv with original column order.

arguments.keystrokes:
cat > /tmp/final.R << 'EOF'
library(bnlearn)
df <- read.csv('/app/bn_sample_10k.csv')
dag <- model2network('[U][Y|U][R|U][D|U:Y][M|U:R]')
a <- arcs(dag)
out <- data.frame(to=a[,'to'], from=a[,'from'])
write.csv(out, '/app/learned_dag.csv', row.names=FALSE, quote=FALSE)
fit <- bn.fit(dag, df)
mut <- mutilated(fit, evidence=list(Y=0))
ma <- arcs(bn.net(mut))
out2 <- data.frame(to=ma[,'to'], from=ma[,'from'])
write.csv(out2, '/app/intervened_dag.csv', row.names=FALSE, quote=FALSE)
set.seed(42)
samp <- rbn(mut, n=10000)
samp <- samp[, c('U','Y','R','D','M')]
write.csv(samp, '/app/final_bn_sample.csv', row.names=FALSE)
cat('done\n')
print(summary(samp))
EOF
Rscript /tmp/final.R
